_meta.indication: For the treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-treatment, 3-period complete crossover study comparing sebetralstat 300 mg and 600 mg to placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adolescents and adults aged 12 years and older with HAE Type I or II.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to beginning of symptom relief defined as at least 'a little better' (2 consecutive timepoints) within 12 hours of first dose, measured by PGI-C.
pivotal_trials.n: 110 subjects; 264 treated attacks (87 with 300 mg, 93 with 600 mg, 84 with placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: Symptom relief within 12 hours achieved by 76% (300 mg), 76% (600 mg) vs 49% (placebo); median time to relief 1.8 h (300 mg) and 2.0 h (600 mg); primary endpoint p<0.0001 (300 mg vs placebo) and p=0.0004 (600 mg vs placebo).

key_safety: Adverse reactions were rare; the most common adverse reaction (incidence ≥2%) was headache, occurring in 3.2% of EKTERLY 600 mg patients vs 1.2% on placebo.
target_moa: Sebetralstat is a competitive, reversible oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor that blocks the kallikrein-kinin pathway, decreasing bradykinin production that mediates HAE attacks.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was held; the application did not raise challenging efficacy or safety issues requiring external input.

summary.text: Sebetralstat was developed under a standard NDA review with Fast Track Designation (November 18, 2019) and Orphan Drug Designation (September 7, 2021) for bradykinin-mediated angioedema; a Breakthrough Therapy request was denied, and it was approved based on a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus confirmatory mechanistic evidence.

citations.quote: Sebetralstat received Fast Track Designation on November 18, 2019, and orphan drug designation on September 7, 2021.

On April 1, 2022, a Breakthrough Therapy request was received, and it was denied on May 25, 2022, because the preliminary clinical evidence submitted does not indicate that KVD900 may demonstrate substantial improvement over existing therapies on one or more clinically significant endpoints.

The substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) of sebetralstat in patients with HAE was established using data from a single adequate and well-controlled trial (Trial 301, “KONFIDENT”, hereafter referred to as Trial 301) and confirmatory evidence (CE) based on mechanistic data (see Section 1.2).
